caption: The video showcases five maroon metronomes standing in a row on a white foam plank that rests on two metal cans lying on their sides as rollers, against a flat teal wall on a light wooden table. Each metronome's thin pendulum rod, with a sliding weight, swings continuously side to side, the rods and weights blurred by motion in many moments. The oscillation is already underway and continues throughout. Over time the relative phases of the rods shift: early on they point in mixed directions, some left, some right, some near vertical. As time passes the right-hand metronomes swing together, crossing vertical at nearly the same moment, while the leftmost unit sometimes lags. The white plank and the two cans stay essentially fixed in position, with no clear horizontal translation or tilt, so the platform serves as a quiet base. Bright specular highlights on the can ends are reflections, and the metronome bodies keep constant spacing throughout, with no object entering or leaving.
relations: Five metronomes swing continuously on a foam plank supported by two cylindrical cans.
The relative phases of the metronome pendulums shift over time, causing partial synchronization.
The white plank and metal cans remain mostly stationary, acting as a stable base.
